legend: Someone give a strange birthday present to Ivan. It is hedgehog — connected undirected graph in which one vertex has degree at least 3%%ZSMJ0%% (we will call it center) and all other vertices has degree 1. Ivan thought that hedgehog is too boring and decided to make himself k%%ZSMJ1%%-multihedgehog.
Let us define k%%ZSMJ2%%-multihedgehog as follows:
1%%ZSMJ3%%-multihedgehog is hedgehog: it has one vertex of degree at least 3%%ZSMJ4%% and some vertices of degree 1.

For all k≥2%%ZSMJ5%%, k%%ZSMJ6%%-multihedgehog is (k−1)%%ZSMJ7%%-multihedgehog in which the following changes has been made for each vertex v%%ZSMJ8%% with degree 1: let u%%ZSMJ9%% be its only neighbor; remove vertex v%%ZSMJ10%%, create a new hedgehog with center at vertex w%%ZSMJ11%% and connect vertices u%%ZSMJ12%% and w%%ZSMJ13%% with an edge. New hedgehogs can differ from each other and the initial gift.

Thereby k%%ZSMJ14%%-multihedgehog is a tree. Ivan made k%%ZSMJ15%%-multihedgehog but he is not sure that he did not make any mistakes. That is why he asked you to check if his tree is indeed k%%ZSMJ16%%-multihedgehog.
input: First line of input contains 2%%ZSMJ17%% integers n%%ZSMJ18%%, k%%ZSMJ19%% (1≤n≤105%%ZSMJ20%%, 1≤k≤109%%ZSMJ21%%) — number of vertices and hedgehog parameter.
Next n−1%%ZSMJ22%% lines contains two integers u%%ZSMJ23%% v%%ZSMJ24%% (1≤u,v≤n;u≠v%%ZSMJ25%%) — indices of vertices connected by edge.
It is guaranteed that given graph is a tree.
output: Print "Yes" (without quotes), if given graph is k%%ZSMJ26%%-multihedgehog, and "No" (without quotes) otherwise.
note: 2-multihedgehog from the first example looks like this:
Its center is vertex 13%%ZSMJ27%%. Hedgehogs created on last step are: [4 (center), 1, 2, 3], [6 (center), 7, 8, 9], [5 (center), 10, 11, 12, 13].
Tree from second example is not a hedgehog because degree of center should be at least 3%%ZSMJ28%%.
